import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 25: Logarithmic density of size-dependent congruences

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/25](https://www.erdosproblems.com/25)
-/

open Filter Finset Real Nat Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos25

/--
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_25 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ i, 0 < seq_n i) → StrictMono seq_n →
      ∃ d, Set.HasLogDensity
        { x : ℕ | ∀ i, (x : ℤ) < seq_n i ∨ ¬((x : ℤ) ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD seq_n i]) } d := by
  sorry

end Erdos25

reformulations.difference: The formalization includes 0 in its natural-number set and logarithmic-density sum, and divides each summand by log N rather than normalizing a sum over positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In Lean, the zero summand is zero. The scratch file proves, for every A and d, that A.HasLogDensity d is equivalent to convergence of (1 / log N) times the sum of 1/k over k ∈ A ∩ {1,…,N}. The exceptional normalization values at N=0,1 do not affect convergence at infinity. In particular, when the first modulus is 1, Lean's set is {0} rather than the empty positive-integer set; both have logarithmic density 0, as also verified in Lean.
